about: Clues for Word Search at level 4, written for this app at about a 2nd to 3rd grade reading level. For each theme in search-themes.json, one short clue per word (44 characters at most) that points to the word without using it, and that fits only that word among the theme's 16.

On the Farm.cow: It gives milk and says moo.
On the Farm.pig: A pink animal that says oink.
On the Farm.horse: A big, fast animal you ride with a saddle.
On the Farm.sheep: A woolly animal that says baa.
On the Farm.goat: It has horns and a little beard.
On the Farm.duck: A bird that swims and says quack.
On the Farm.hen: A mother chicken that lays eggs.
On the Farm.barn: A big red building for farm animals.
On the Farm.mule: It looks like a horse with long ears.
On the Farm.goose: A big white bird that says honk.
On the Farm.pony: A small horse just right for kids.
On the Farm.turkey: A big bird that says gobble gobble.

In the Ocean.fish: Most kinds have fins, scales, and gills.
In the Ocean.shark: A big fish with rows of sharp teeth.
In the Ocean.whale: The biggest animal in the sea.
In the Ocean.crab: It walks sideways and has two claws.
In the Ocean.seal: It barks and has flippers and whiskers.
In the Ocean.wave: Water that rolls up onto the beach.
In the Ocean.shell: A sea snail's hard home, found on sand.
In the Ocean.squid: It has ten arms and squirts ink.
In the Ocean.eel: A long fish that looks like a snake.
In the Ocean.coral: Tiny animals build this colorful reef.
In the Ocean.starfish: A sea animal with five pointy arms.
In the Ocean.octopus: A sea animal with eight arms.
In the Ocean.dolphin: A smart sea animal that leaps and clicks.
In the Ocean.boat: You ride in it to float on water.
In the Ocean.tide: The sea rises and falls twice a day.
In the Ocean.clam: It lives in sand between two shells.

Weather.rain: Drops of water that fall from clouds.
Weather.snow: Soft white flakes that fall in winter.
Weather.wind: Fast moving air that can fly a kite.
Weather.cloud: A puffy white shape up in the sky.
Weather.sunny: Bright and clear, with blue skies.
Weather.fog: A thick mist that is hard to see in.
Weather.hail: Hard balls of ice that fall from the sky.
Weather.frost: Thin white ice on grass in the morning.
Weather.rainbow: An arch of colors in the sky.
Weather.cold: How ice feels when you touch it.
Weather.warm: A little bit hot, like a cozy blanket.
Weather.breeze: A soft, gentle puff of air.
Weather.puddle: A small pool of water to splash in.

Fruit.apple: A round red fruit with a core.
Fruit.pear: A green fruit that is wide at the bottom.
Fruit.plum: A smooth purple fruit with one big pit.
Fruit.grape: A small round fruit that grows on a vine.
Fruit.peach: A fuzzy fruit with one big pit.
Fruit.mango: A sweet fruit with one big flat seed.
Fruit.kiwi: A fuzzy brown fruit that is green inside.
Fruit.melon: A big heavy fruit with a hard rind.
Fruit.cherry: A tiny red fruit with a long stem.
Fruit.banana: A long yellow fruit you peel.
Fruit.orange: A round fruit named for its color.
Fruit.berry: A tiny juicy fruit that grows on a bush.
Fruit.fig: A small soft fruit baked into bar cookies.
Fruit.papaya: A big fruit with many black seeds inside.

Vegetables.corn: Yellow kernels that grow on a cob.
Vegetables.peas: Little green balls that grow in a pod.
Vegetables.bean: A long, thin green pod you snap and eat.
Vegetables.carrot: A crunchy orange root rabbits like.
Vegetables.potato: It grows underground and makes fries.
Vegetables.onion: It can make you cry when you cut it.
Vegetables.kale: Dark green curly leaves you can eat.
Vegetables.beet: A dark red root that stains your hands.
Vegetables.squash: A pumpkin is one kind of this.
Vegetables.pepper: A bell-shaped veggie, red or green.
Vegetables.lettuce: Light green leaves used in most salads.
Vegetables.garlic: A strong-smelling bulb made of cloves.
Vegetables.radish: A small red root with a spicy bite.
Vegetables.yam: An orange root, like a sweet potato.
Vegetables.tomato: A red, juicy one used to make ketchup.

At School.book: It has pages full of words and stories.
At School.desk: A table where you sit to do your work.
At School.pencil: You write with it and can sharpen it.
At School.paper: A thin white sheet you write on.
At School.ruler: It helps you measure and draw lines.
At School.glue: It is sticky and holds things together.
At School.chalk: A white stick for writing on a board.
At School.teacher: The grown-up who helps you learn.
At School.lunch: The meal you eat at noon.
At School.class: A group of kids who learn together.
At School.crayon: A wax stick you color with.
At School.read: What you do with the words in a story.
At School.spell: To put letters in the right order.

Outer Space.sun: It gives us light and heat each day.
Outer Space.moon: It glows at night and changes shape.
Outer Space.star: A tiny point of light in the night sky.
Outer Space.planet: Eight of these go around our sun.
Outer Space.comet: A ball of ice with a long glowing tail.
Outer Space.rocket: It blasts off and carries astronauts.
Outer Space.orbit: The path a world takes around its sun.
Outer Space.earth: The world where we all live.
Outer Space.mars: A red world where robot rovers drive.
Outer Space.space: The huge, dark place beyond the sky.
Outer Space.galaxy: The Milky Way is one of these.
Outer Space.crater: A round hole on the moon's ground.
Outer Space.saturn: A giant world with bright rings.
Outer Space.venus: The hottest world, second from the sun.
Outer Space.launch: To send a ship up after the countdown.
Outer Space.meteor: A streak of light called a shooting star.

In the Kitchen.pot: A deep one with a lid for making soup.
In the Kitchen.pan: A flat one for frying eggs.
In the Kitchen.fork: It has pointy tines to poke your food.
In the Kitchen.cup: You drink milk or juice from it.
In the Kitchen.plate: A flat dish that holds your dinner.
In the Kitchen.bowl: A deep round dish for cereal.
In the Kitchen.oven: A hot box where cakes and cookies bake.
In the Kitchen.sink: You wash dishes here under a faucet.
In the Kitchen.stove: It has burners on top to cook on.
In the Kitchen.mixer: A machine that spins to blend batter.
In the Kitchen.apron: You wear it to keep your clothes clean.
In the Kitchen.toast: Bread that is browned and crunchy.
In the Kitchen.kettle: It whistles when the water boils.
In the Kitchen.napkin: You wipe your mouth with it.
In the Kitchen.whisk: A wire tool you use by hand to beat eggs.

Bugs.ant: A small bug that carries crumbs in a line.
Bugs.moth: It flies at night toward porch lights.
Bugs.wasp: A thin bug with a tiny waist that stings.
Bugs.flea: A tiny jumper that makes dogs itch.
Bugs.beetle: A six-legged bug with hard wing covers.
Bugs.spider: It has eight legs and spins a web.
Bugs.cricket: It chirps at night by rubbing its wings.
Bugs.ladybug: A red bug with black spots.
Bugs.firefly: Its tail glows and blinks at night.
Bugs.worm: It has no legs and wiggles in dirt.
Bugs.snail: A slow crawler with a house on its back.
Bugs.gnat: A tiny fly that swarms near your face.
Bugs.hornet: The biggest kind of stinging bug.
Bugs.termite: A tiny bug that eats wood.
Bugs.cicada: It buzzes loudly in trees in summer.

My Body.arm: It goes from your shoulder to your wrist.
My Body.leg: Your thigh and shin are parts of it.
My Body.hand: It has a palm, and you wave with it.
My Body.foot: It has a heel and fits in a shoe.
My Body.head: Your hair grows on top of it.
My Body.knee: The joint in the middle of your leg.
My Body.elbow: The joint where your arm bends.
My Body.chin: The bottom of your face, under your lips.
My Body.neck: It joins your head to your shoulders.
My Body.toe: You have ten, and they wiggle in socks.
My Body.thumb: The short, thick one beside your pointer.
My Body.finger: You point with it and wear a ring on it.
My Body.ankle: The joint just above your heel.

Sports.ball: A round thing you throw, catch, or bounce.
Sports.bat: A wooden stick for hitting in baseball.
Sports.goal: You shoot at it while a keeper guards it.
Sports.kick: To hit something hard with your foot.
Sports.swim: To move through water in a pool.
Sports.run: To move fast on your feet.
Sports.race: A contest to see who is fastest.
Sports.skate: To glide on ice with blades on your feet.
Sports.ski: To slide down a snowy hill on two boards.
Sports.team: A group that plays on the same side.
Sports.score: The numbers that tell who is winning.
Sports.soccer: A game where only the goalie uses hands.
Sports.tennis: A game with rackets and a fuzzy ball.
Sports.hockey: A game on ice with sticks and a puck.
Sports.net: Mesh strung across the middle of a court.
Sports.jump: To push off the ground into the air.

Colors.red: The color of a stop sign.
Colors.blue: The color of a clear daytime sky.
Colors.green: The color of grass and leaves.
Colors.yellow: The color of a lemon or a school bus.
Colors.pink: A light rosy color, like a flamingo.
Colors.orange: The color of a pumpkin or a carrot.
Colors.black: The color of coal and a dark night.
Colors.white: The color of fresh snow and milk.
Colors.brown: The color of chocolate and mud.
Colors.gray: The color of an elephant or a rain cloud.
Colors.gold: A shiny yellow, like a first-place medal.
Colors.silver: The shiny color of a new dime or a spoon.
Colors.tan: A light sandy color, like a beach.
Colors.teal: A dark blue-green, like a peacock.
Colors.violet: A color named for a small spring flower.

Clothes.hat: Worn on your head, often with a wide brim.
Clothes.cap: It has a bill in front, worn for baseball.
Clothes.coat: A long, heavy layer for cold winter days.
Clothes.sock: It goes on your foot before your sneaker.
Clothes.shoe: It ties with laces and goes on your foot.
Clothes.boot: It is tall and keeps feet dry in snow.
Clothes.shirt: A top with sleeves, like a tee or a polo.
Clothes.pants: They cover both legs down to your ankles.
Clothes.dress: One piece with a top and a skirt part.
Clothes.scarf: You wrap it around your neck.
Clothes.glove: It covers your hand and each finger.
Clothes.mitten: It keeps four fingers together and warm.
Clothes.jacket: A short, light layer with a zipper.
Clothes.belt: It goes around your waist to hold pants up.
Clothes.vest: A top with no sleeves, worn over another.
Clothes.skirt: It hangs from your waist and twirls.

Music.drum: You hit it with sticks to make a boom.
Music.horn: A curled brass one you blow to go toot.
Music.flute: A thin silver pipe you blow across.
Music.harp: It is tall, and you pluck its many strings.
Music.piano: It has black and white keys.
Music.violin: You play it with a bow under your chin.
Music.tuba: A huge brass one with very low sounds.
Music.song: Words and a tune put together.
Music.sing: To make music with your voice.
Music.band: A group that plays music together.
Music.note: One musical sound, like do or mi.
Music.beat: The steady pulse you clap along to.
Music.bell: It rings ding-dong when it swings.
Music.banjo: A twangy string thing with a round body.
Music.guitar: It has six strings and you strum it.
Music.choir: A group of people using only voices.

Camping.tent: A cloth shelter you sleep in.
Camping.fire: It is hot and crackles as wood burns.
Camping.log: A thick piece of a fallen trunk.
Camping.map: A drawing that shows where places are.
Camping.trail: A path you follow through the woods.
Camping.lake: A big body of water with land all around.
Camping.lantern: A lamp with a handle to carry at night.
Camping.forest: A huge area of woods where animals live.
Camping.trees: Tall plants with trunks and leaves.
Camping.stars: Tiny lights that twinkle in the night sky.
Camping.cabin: A small wooden house in the woods.
Camping.owl: A night bird that says hoo.
Camping.marsh: Soft, wet land full of reeds and frogs.

Birds.owl: It hoots at night and has big eyes.
Birds.crow: A big black bird that says caw.
Birds.robin: A bird with a red chest that eats worms.
Birds.eagle: A huge, mighty bird with a white head.
Birds.hawk: A fast hunting bird with a red tail.
Birds.duck: It quacks and swims in a pond.
Birds.swan: A big white bird with a long, curved neck.
Birds.dove: A soft white bird that stands for peace.
Birds.wren: A tiny brown bird with a tail that tips up.
Birds.jay: A noisy blue bird with a pointy crest.
Birds.parrot: A bright bird that can copy what you say.
Birds.pigeon: A gray bird that walks around city parks.
Birds.finch: A small yellow bird that cracks seeds.
Birds.goose: It honks and flies south in a V shape.
Birds.heron: A tall bird that wades on long, thin legs.
Birds.penguin: A black and white bird that cannot fly.

Jobs.chef: This person cooks meals in a restaurant.
Jobs.nurse: The school helper you see if you feel sick.
Jobs.farmer: This person grows crops and raises cows.
Jobs.baker: This person makes bread and cupcakes.
Jobs.vet: This person helps sick pets feel better.
Jobs.judge: This person is in charge of a courtroom.
Jobs.coach: This person leads a sports team.
Jobs.doctor: This person listens to your heart beat.
Jobs.artist: This person draws and makes clay shapes.
Jobs.dentist: This person checks and cleans your teeth.
Jobs.author: This person writes books.
Jobs.singer: This person uses their voice to make music.
Jobs.painter: This person uses a brush to color walls.
Jobs.teacher: This person helps a class learn at school.
Jobs.mayor: This person is the leader of a town or city.

Going Places.car: A small ride with four wheels and a trunk.
Going Places.bus: A long yellow one takes kids to school.
Going Places.train: It rides on rails and says choo choo.
Going Places.plane: It has wings and takes off at an airport.
Going Places.boat: A small thing that floats; you can row it.
Going Places.ship: It is huge and sails across the ocean.
Going Places.bike: It has two wheels and pedals.
Going Places.truck: It hauls big loads in the back.
Going Places.van: A boxy ride with sliding side doors.
Going Places.taxi: You pay its driver to take you somewhere.
Going Places.jet: The fastest kind of flyer, with a loud roar.
Going Places.tractor: A farmer drives this to pull a plow.
Going Places.wagon: A little red one that kids pull by a handle.
Going Places.subway: It zips through tunnels under a city.
Going Places.scooter: You stand on it and push with one foot.

In the Garden.seed: You plant this tiny thing to grow a flower.
In the Garden.soil: The dirt that plants grow in.
In the Garden.root: The part of a plant that grows underground.
In the Garden.stem: The long stalk that holds a flower up.
In the Garden.leaf: A flat green part of a plant.
In the Garden.rose: A flower with thorns that smells sweet.
In the Garden.tulip: A spring flower shaped like a cup.
In the Garden.daisy: A white flower with a yellow center.
In the Garden.weed: A pesky plant that you pull out.
In the Garden.hose: A long tube that sprays water.
In the Garden.rake: A tool with teeth for gathering leaves.
In the Garden.sprout: A baby plant just popping out of the dirt.
In the Garden.bloom: What a flower does when it opens up.
In the Garden.petal: One of the soft, colorful parts of a flower.
In the Garden.worm: A wiggly pink animal that lives in dirt.

Pets.dog: A grown pet that barks and plays fetch.
Pets.cat: A grown pet that purrs and meows.
Pets.fish: A pet with fins and gills, of any size.
Pets.bird: A pet with feathers that sings in a cage.
Pets.frog: A green pet that hops and says ribbit.
Pets.hamster: A small furry pet that runs on a wheel.
Pets.rabbit: A pet with long ears that hops.
Pets.turtle: A slow pet with a hard shell.
Pets.mouse: A tiny squeaky pet with a long thin tail.
Pets.puppy: A baby pet that will grow up to bark.
Pets.kitten: A baby pet that will grow up to meow.
Pets.lizard: A scaly pet with four legs and a long tail.
Pets.parrot: A feathered pet that can learn to talk.
Pets.snake: A long pet with no legs that hisses.
Pets.pony: A small horse that kids can ride.
Pets.guppy: A very tiny swimmer with a fancy tail.

At the Zoo.lion: A big cat with a mane and a loud roar.
At the Zoo.tiger: A big orange cat with black stripes.
At the Zoo.bear: A big brown animal that sleeps all winter.
At the Zoo.zebra: It looks like a horse with stripes.
At the Zoo.camel: It has a hump and walks in the desert.
At the Zoo.monkey: It swings by its tail and eats bananas.
At the Zoo.panda: A black and white animal that eats bamboo.
At the Zoo.hippo: A huge gray animal that stays in the river.
At the Zoo.rhino: A big gray animal with a horn on its nose.
At the Zoo.giraffe: The tallest animal, with a very long neck.
At the Zoo.koala: A fuzzy gray tree hugger from Australia.
At the Zoo.otter: It floats on its back and cracks shells.
At the Zoo.seal: It claps its flippers and barks.
At the Zoo.llama: A woolly animal with a long neck that spits.
At the Zoo.moose: A huge deer with wide, flat antlers.
At the Zoo.gorilla: The biggest ape; it beats on its chest.

At the Beach.sand: Tiny grains you use to build a castle.
At the Beach.sun: It shines in the sky and warms you up.
At the Beach.wave: A roll of water that crashes on the shore.
At the Beach.towel: You dry off with this after a dip.
At the Beach.shell: A sea animal's hard home you can collect.
At the Beach.shovel: A small tool for digging holes.
At the Beach.kite: It flies in the wind on a long string.
At the Beach.crab: It has claws and walks sideways.
At the Beach.gull: A white sea bird that steals your snacks.
At the Beach.swim: To move through water with arms and legs.
At the Beach.dune: A hill made by the wind near the shore.
At the Beach.tide: It makes the sea rise and fall each day.
At the Beach.umbrella: It gives you shade on a bright day.
At the Beach.surf: To ride the water standing on a board.

Winter.snow: White stuff you can roll into big balls.
Winter.sled: You sit on it and zoom down a hill.
Winter.skate: To glide on a frozen pond in special shoes.
Winter.ice: Frozen water that is hard and slippery.
Winter.scarf: You wrap it around your neck.
Winter.mitten: A warm hand cover with only a thumb part.
Winter.cocoa: A sweet chocolate drink in a warm mug.
Winter.frost: Thin white crystals on your window at dawn.
Winter.igloo: A dome house built from frozen blocks.
Winter.boots: Tall shoes that keep your feet dry.
Winter.coat: A thick jacket with sleeves and a zipper.
Winter.flake: One tiny white crystal; no two are alike.
Winter.chilly: A word for when the air feels a bit cool.
Winter.shovel: A tool for clearing the driveway.
Winter.hat: It keeps your head and ears warm.

Breakfast.egg: A hen lays it; you can fry or scramble it.
Breakfast.toast: Bread cooked until brown and crisp.
Breakfast.milk: A white drink that comes from cows.
Breakfast.juice: A sweet drink squeezed from fruit.
Breakfast.cereal: You pour it in a bowl and eat with a spoon.
Breakfast.bacon: Thin, salty strips of meat fried in a pan.
Breakfast.waffle: A breakfast cake with little squares.
Breakfast.muffin: It looks like a cupcake with no frosting.
Breakfast.yogurt: A cool, creamy food in a little cup.
Breakfast.oats: The grain in a warm bowl of porridge.
Breakfast.jam: A sweet fruit spread, like strawberry.
Breakfast.butter: A soft yellow spread made from cream.
Breakfast.bagel: A round, chewy bread with a hole.
Breakfast.honey: A sweet, golden food made by bees.
Breakfast.syrup: A sticky brown topping from maple trees.
Breakfast.pancake: A flat, round treat you flip as it cooks.

Playground Fun.slide: You go up the steps and zoom down it.
Playground Fun.swing: A seat on chains that goes back and forth.
Playground Fun.seesaw: One kid goes up as the other goes down.
Playground Fun.sandbox: A place to dig and build castles.
Playground Fun.ladder: You go up it one rung at a time.
Playground Fun.climb: To go up using your hands and feet.
Playground Fun.bench: A long seat where grown-ups sit and watch.
Playground Fun.ramp: A slanted path with no steps.
Playground Fun.chalk: You draw on the sidewalk with it.
Playground Fun.rope: You can jump over it or tug on it.
Playground Fun.ball: A round toy you kick, throw, or bounce.
Playground Fun.run: To move your legs very fast.
Playground Fun.fort: A hideout with walls, like a little castle.
Playground Fun.friend: Someone you like to play with.

Birthday Party.cake: A sweet dessert you slice and share.
Birthday Party.candle: You blow out its little flame.
Birthday Party.balloon: It is full of air and floats on a string.
Birthday Party.gift: A four-letter word for a wrapped surprise.
Birthday Party.present: A seven-letter word for a wrapped surprise.
Birthday Party.party: A fun time with guests, food, and music.
Birthday Party.hat: A paper cone you wear on your head.
Birthday Party.card: Folded paper with a note inside.
Birthday Party.games: Fun things to play, like musical chairs.
Birthday Party.wish: You make one in secret with your eyes shut.
Birthday Party.friends: Pals you invite over to play.
Birthday Party.candy: Sweet treats like lollipops and gummies.
Birthday Party.ribbon: A long, thin strip tied around a box.
Birthday Party.bow: A pretty knot with two loops.
Birthday Party.song: A happy tune with words, just for you.
Birthday Party.icing: The sweet, creamy topping you lick off.

The Rainforest.jungle: A thick, wild forest full of animals.
The Rainforest.vine: A long plant that hangs like a rope.
The Rainforest.tree: A tall plant with a trunk and branches.
The Rainforest.frog: It hops and croaks, and starts as a tadpole.
The Rainforest.parrot: A bright bird that can copy words.
The Rainforest.sloth: A very slow animal that hangs upside down.
The Rainforest.toucan: A bird with a huge, colorful beak.
The Rainforest.monkey: It swings on branches and eats bananas.
The Rainforest.snake: A long animal with no legs that slithers.
The Rainforest.rain: Water drops that fall from clouds.
The Rainforest.leaf: A flat green part that grows on a branch.
The Rainforest.moss: A soft green fuzz that grows on logs.
The Rainforest.orchid: A fancy flower that grows on branches.
The Rainforest.gecko: A small lizard with sticky toes.
The Rainforest.canopy: The roof of the forest, way up high.

In the Desert.sand: Tiny grains that cover the ground.
In the Desert.cactus: A prickly plant that stores water.
In the Desert.camel: An animal with a hump that people ride.
In the Desert.lizard: A small scaly animal with four legs.
In the Desert.snake: It has no legs and may rattle its tail.
In the Desert.dune: A big hill piled up by the wind.
In the Desert.sun: The bright star that lights up the day.
In the Desert.oasis: A green spot with water and palm trees.
In the Desert.coyote: A wild dog that howls at night.
In the Desert.hawk: A bird that hunts from high in the sky.
In the Desert.rock: A hard chunk of stone you can pick up.
In the Desert.tortoise: A slow animal with a heavy shell.
In the Desert.heat: The warmth you feel from a fire or stove.

Arctic Animals.bear: A huge white animal that hunts on the ice.
Arctic Animals.walrus: It has two long tusks and whiskers.
Arctic Animals.seal: A sleek swimmer with flippers and no tusks.
Arctic Animals.fox: A small, sly hunter with a fluffy tail.
Arctic Animals.whale: The name for the biggest animals in the sea.
Arctic Animals.narwhal: A sea animal with one long, twisty tusk.
Arctic Animals.orca: A black and white sea hunter with a big fin.
Arctic Animals.hare: It looks like a big rabbit with long ears.
Arctic Animals.wolf: A wild animal that howls in a pack.
Arctic Animals.reindeer: It pulls a sleigh in holiday stories.
Arctic Animals.puffin: A small sea bird with a bright orange beak.
Arctic Animals.caribou: A wild deer that travels in huge herds.
Arctic Animals.tern: A sea bird that flies from pole to pole.
Arctic Animals.husky: A fluffy dog that pulls a sled.

Dinosaur Days.fossil: A very old print or shape left in stone.
Dinosaur Days.bone: One hard piece of a skeleton.
Dinosaur Days.egg: A baby dino hatches out of this.
Dinosaur Days.claw: A sharp, curved nail on a foot.
Dinosaur Days.tail: The long part at the back end of an animal.
Dinosaur Days.horn: A hard point on the head of a triceratops.
Dinosaur Days.teeth: Sharp things in a mouth for chewing.
Dinosaur Days.roar: A very loud, deep animal sound.
Dinosaur Days.nest: A safe, cozy place where babies hatch.
Dinosaur Days.swamp: Wet, muddy land with lots of plants.
Dinosaur Days.giant: A word for something very, very big.
Dinosaur Days.extinct: A word for animals that are all gone now.
Dinosaur Days.raptor: A small, fast dino that hunted in packs.
Dinosaur Days.scales: Small, hard plates that cover reptile skin.
Dinosaur Days.volcano: A mountain that shoots out lava.
Dinosaur Days.stomp: To walk with loud, heavy steps.

Fun Shapes.circle: A flat round shape, like a coin.
Fun Shapes.square: A boxy shape with four equal sides.
Fun Shapes.star: A shape with five points that twinkles.
Fun Shapes.heart: The shape that stands for love.
Fun Shapes.diamond: A shape like a kite or a shiny gem.
Fun Shapes.cube: A solid shape like a block or dice.
Fun Shapes.cone: It holds a scoop of ice cream.

Number Words.three: How many sides a triangle has.
Number Words.four: How many legs a dog has.
Number Words.five: How many fingers are on a hand.
